entries.name: random_id
entries.canon: messages.createChat#92ceddd4 flags:# users:Vector<InputUser> title:string ttl_period:flags.0?int = messages.InvitedUsers (api.tl LAYER 229:2507)
entries.reason: messages.createChat has no random_id, unlike messages.sendMessage which does. A retry after a lost response therefore creates a second chat, and canon offers the client no way to say 'this is the same request'. The field is a SETNX-keyed Redis dedup with a 600s window so a retry inside it returns the same chat_id; a client that does not send it gets canon's behaviour unchanged, which is duplicate chats on retry.

entries.name: MintDownloadToken
entries.reason: No upload.mintDownloadToken in api.tl; this mints ImpulseM's own short-TTL signed browser-download token, a mechanism real TL clients never need since they never do a bare HTTPS download.

entries.name: refresh_token
entries.canon: auth.authorization#2ea2c0d4 flags:# setup_password_required:flags.1?true otherwise_relogin_days:flags.1?int tmp_sessions:flags.0?int future_auth_token:flags.2?bytes user:User = auth.Authorization (api.tl LAYER 229:238)
entries.reason: JWT session mechanism: Canon carries identity in the MTProto auth_key established by the DH handshake -- in the TRANSPORT, not in the response body, which is why auth.authorization has no token field. ImpulseM's client transport is gRPC, which has no auth_key, so the signed session token has nowhere else to arrive. This follows from the board's transport decision, not from a shortcut.
